invariant: The invoked errmsg helper requires compilation errors for missing/repeated labels, jumps into blocks and jumps over local/global declarations including repeat-until locals.

Forward/backward labels, multiple labels, end-of-block declaration jumps and a generated400-byte label program execute with their expected control flow; intentionally unreachable error calls remain unreachable.
Backward jumps reinitialize local registers and retain live values correctly; compile-only infinite-loop bodies remain unreachable through the outer escape.
The six retained closures share or detach each a/b/c/d capture according to the actual crossed lexical scopes; debug.upvalueid distinguishes every required sharing relation.

All five testG branches select their expected return. Gotos around a to-be-closed local preserve its truthy value on in-scope jumps and make that local name unavailable after scope exit. The supplied close callback resets its named global; the later not-varX assertion itself checks name visibility, not that global side effect.
The invoked checkerr helper rejects undeclared/global-close/_ENV errors with source names, while declared globals can shadow locals only in their intended scope.
Default LUA_COMPAT_GLOBAL=1 permits global as an ordinary identifier in the loaded program and emits its reserved-word diagnostic witness.
The upstream-test lexer reserves global; compilation of the same ordinary identifier program fails without executing it.

Global functions recurse through their declared global binding; local shadowing survives; const globals reject assignment/function syntax at correct source lines; wildcard const/read-write transitions preserve actual globals.
Programs generated with1000 global declarations or200 alternating global/local declarations compile and return the actual final values, including names beyond constant/register shortcut ranges.
Global initializers preserve multires adjustment, nil fill, visibility of outer locals and cleanup. A generated300-constant function initializes the explicitly supplied _ENV with actual named values.
Redefining already-present globals raises the expected named runtime errors even for false values in a replaced _ENV. Terminal OK follows the generated and runtime-error tests.
